Revision: 5abbefa5f753ee9a1920d6d2eaeede981e79eeff
License used: Apache-2.0 (upstream license files retained)
Original file SHA256 values: UPSTREAM.json

Android NativeActivity recreation:
- Keep AndroidPlatform in render-thread local storage, return owned Arc clones,
  and release that slot on the same thread when its event loop ends.
- Replace the process AndroidApp handle for each Activity. Pin a JNI local
  Activity reference before releasing a handle clone so concurrent recreation
  cannot invalidate an in-flight JNI call. Remove the unused bare Activity
  pointer accessor; callers can retain android_app() or use activity().
- Reset deferred lifecycle/readiness and chrome-cache flags for each renderer.
  Publish initialized only after the first frame, matching the readiness API.
- Keep the existing NativeActivity event/ACK protocol. No thread unsafe Send
  additions, skipped lifecycle acknowledgements, or process restart workaround.

Changed upstream files: src/android/jni.rs and src/android/window.rs.
Added local helper: src/android/surface_lifecycle.rs.
The iOS backend and other upstream source files are unchanged.

Bounded native input panel focus:
- Separate real Activity lifecycle from primary/embedded window focus. A child
  text panel can receive IME focus while GPUI continues rendering layout updates.
- A short transfer flag bridges the focus change. Actual panel focus loss clears
  it, and Activity Pause always overrides every focus bit.
- JNI copies only atomic focus state; no Activity lifecycle/ACK is synthesized.

Android surface teardown and recreation:
- TerminateWindow synchronously stops use of and detaches the old renderer
  surface before returning the callback's native-window destruction ACK. The
  device, queue, atlas and pipelines remain available for the next window.
- InitWindow and resize work remain deferred; the synchronous teardown path
  does not call AndroidApp accessors or wait for Java/UI work.
- Failed surface initialization does not publish readiness. The local lifecycle
  helper permits retry after 250 ms, cancels stale init/retry work on termination,
  and resets the old backoff when a new InitWindow arrives.
- Each attachment resets its first-presented-frame state. The JNI readiness
  flag is published only after renderer.draw actually reaches presentation;
  an empty scene, absent callback or deferred/failed frame cannot mark it ready.
- The helper's three policy regressions pass. The rebuilt Android APK passes
  four same-Activity CREATED -> RESUMED cycles with readiness=false when detached,
  successful-first-present readiness and panel/title pixel assertions on the
  default host-GPU emulator path. Physical-device recovery and Vulkan rendering
  itself remain unverified or unresolved; see docs/p0-android-2026-11-06.md.
